metadata.summary: Britain's Jodie Burrage has received death threats and abuse on social media after she was beaten in the first round of the Chennai Open on Tuesday.
metadata.content: Jodie Burrage: British player receives death threats and abuse on social media after Chennai Open first-round defeat | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Jodie Burrage: British player receives death threats and abuse on social media after Chennai Open first-round defeat Jodie Burrage has revealed online abuse and death threats; both Burrage and fellow British player Katie Boulter believe most abuse comes from tennis gamblers who have lost money; Warning: This article contains details some readers may find distressing Tuesday 3 November 2026 22:34, UK Image: Jodie Burrage has received death threats and abuse on social media following her defeat at the Chennai Open Britain's Jodie Burrage has received death threats and abuse on social media after she was beaten in the first round of the Chennai Open on Tuesday. Burrage, who was playing her first WTA Tour singles match in 16 months, went down against India's Vaishnavi Adkar. She looked poised for victory when she led 5-3 in the deciding set but lost four games in a row to fall to a 3-6 6-3 7-5 defeat after two hours and 47 minutes. The 27-year-old, who reached a career-high ranking 85 in September 2023, published an Instagram story with some of the abuse received due to the defeat. Ferrari Academy driver Camara, who had already been announced to take Ocon's seat from the start of 2027, will become an F1 driver earlier than anticipated.
